correctness.rationale: Every integer quadratic admits an integral Newton expansion with coefficients determined by values at 0, e_i, 2e_i and e_i+e_j. Minimal common prime-valuation of actual values divides all Newton coefficients, giving a nonzero reduction modulo p. For odd p the total degree-two field bound gives support at least (p-2)/p; for 2, independent u=x mod2 and v=floor(x/2) mod2 bits give a Boolean quadratic with support at least 1/4, or affine at least 1/2 for n=1. For exponent one, B_i=2a_i yields the same bound. CRT reduces global support to any nonzero local component; explicit m/p times x(x-1), x, or x1x2 exactly attain the minimum. All cases m>=2,n>=1 covered. Companion checker exhausts 450011 finite coefficient arrays in 16 cases and 297 CRT witness cases; no finite enumeration substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The exact last-gap problem is explicitly highlighted as a future direction in arXiv:1404.4852 §8, which conjectures only the 2-power pattern and describes mixed moduli as difficult. This theorem proves the conjecture for every n and exponent and completely resolves the degree-two sharp extremal gap for all residue rings, giving a structural 2-adic Newton/Boolean plus CRT mechanism. It is a mathematically motivated natural sharp classification, not a routine finite enumeration.
